sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added with the nightshades work (2026-10-17): every character from the floras in the nightshades notes (plantgen-claude project-files/nightshades/SOURCES.md), drawn by the rules its taxa hold; drawing values only where no character says them.

taxon.note: WCVP v16 accepted name Datura stramonium, plant_name_id 2757848 (Library 1.0 list, read 2026-10-17).

growth_form.note: Its habit as the floras describe it, drawn by the forb form.

growth.note: Grown to the age it is drawn at: an annual's one season, a perennial's or shrub's few years.

variants.note: One seed in the open, as the built-in species.

generator.params.note: Drawing values no character gives (nightshades, 2026-10-17): one plant from one seed; a stout stem (Britton and Brown) 18 mm at the foot and six leaves below the first fork, by eye from photographs (iNaturalist 54718314).

allometry.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 2, Stramonium, p. 1838 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): 2 or 3 ft or more in rich soil; Britton and Brown 1-5 ft; Bentham 1-2 ft; Wikipedia 2-5 ft. Its reference height is the middle of that range, 0.9 m, at its last keyframe.

traits.life_span.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Datura stramonium, c. p. 170 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): an annual.

traits.height_typical_m.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 2, Stramonium, p. 1838 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): 2 or 3 ft or more in rich soil; Britton and Brown 1-5 ft; Bentham 1-2 ft; Wikipedia 2-5 ft.

traits.sympodial_unit_leaves.note: Wikipedia, 'Datura stramonium' (read 2026-10-17): the stem forks repeatedly, each fork producing a leaf and a single erect flower; King's: leaves arise from the forks.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Datura stramonium, c. p. 170 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): leaves ovate in outline, acute or acuminate, mostly narrowed at the base.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Datura stramonium, c. p. 170 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): irregularly sinuate-lobed with acute lobes; Bentham: irregular angular or pointed teeth or lobes.

traits.leaf_margin.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 2, Stramonium, p. 1838 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): variously and sharply sinuate-toothed; Gray p. 717: sinuate-toothed or angled.

traits.leaf_apex.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Datura stramonium, c. p. 170 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): acute or acuminate.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Datura stramonium, c. p. 170 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): leaves 3-8 in long; Wikipedia the same.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Datura stramonium, c. p. 170 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): petioles 1-4 in.

traits.leaf_colour.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 2, Stramonium, p. 1838 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): dark green above, paler beneath. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.bark_colour.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 2, Stramonium, p. 1838 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): stem yellowish green; Gray: green-stemmed. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Datura stramonium, c. p. 170 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): limb 1-1.5 in broad (partly unreadable).

traits.corolla_tube_length_m.note: Gray's New Manual, 7th ed. (1908), Datura stramonium, p. 717 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): corolla 7-9 cm long, its 5 lobes short teeth (Bentham: narrow teeth), so the tube is the corolla's length less a centimetre; Britton and Brown: about 4 in high; Wikipedia 2.5-3.5 in.

traits.flower_posture.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Datura stramonium, c. p. 170 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): flowers erect, short-peduncled; King's: axillary and erect; Wikipedia: a single erect flower in each fork.

traits.flower_colour.note: Gray's New Manual, 7th ed. (1908), Datura stramonium, p. 717 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): corolla white; Britton and Brown: white or violet. The colour is our reading of the word.

traits.petal_apex.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Datura, c. p. 170 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): limb of broad, acuminate lobes; King's: tipped with short points.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Datura stramonium, c. p. 170 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): capsule ovoid, about 2 in high; Wikipedia 1-3 in.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 2, Stramonium, p. 1838 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): a large dry capsule. The brown is our reading of a dry capsule; no source names its colour.

traits.fruit_posture.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Datura stramonium, c. p. 170 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): capsule held upright; Bailey: capsule erect.

traits.flowering_months.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Datura stramonium, c. p. 170 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): June-September; King's July-September.

traits.fruiting_months.note: Capsules ripen after the flowers, through late summer and autumn (Bentham, Gray: flowering summer and autumn); months our reading.

traits.fruit_armature.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Datura stramonium, c. p. 170 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): capsule ovoid, densely prickly; Gray (p. 717) and Bentham: prickly.

traits.calyx_in_fruit.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 3 (1913), Datura stramonium, c. p. 170 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): the capsule held upright above the persistent calyx-base; Bentham: the calyx breaks off round its base, leaving a rim under the capsule.

traits.capsule_valves.note: Gray's New Manual, 7th ed. (1908), Datura (genus account), p. 717 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): capsule prickly, more or less 4-celled, 4-valved; Britton and Brown (vol. 3, c. p. 170, genus account): 4-valved from the top, or bursting irregularly in other species.
